long_biography.plain_text:
Cinema interested Charles Steven Cohen long before it became a business. He studied English at Tufts and attended Brooklyn Law School with entertainment law in mind, but began in Chemical Bank's real-estate division and joined Cohen Brothers Realty in 1979. There he learned leasing, management, construction, financing and development before shifting the group towards acquiring and repositioning commercial properties.

Film eventually became a parallel platform rather than a replacement for real estate. After producing Frozen River, he established Cohen Media Group to distribute contemporary and classic cinema. The business expanded into film rights and theatrical exhibition, including the restoration of Manhattan's Quad Cinema and the purchase of Landmark Theatres. His property experience also shaped an interest in design-led public spaces, visible in the company's design centres across several American markets.
